claims.text: The cast alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and undergoes pesting during high-temperature exposure in air.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a thin, continuous alumina coating by CVD on the as-cast alloy surface.
A CVD alumina coating will significantly improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed coating will not compromise the alloy's room-temperature mechanical properties.
The proposed coating will not compromise the alloy's high-temperature mechanical properties.
The deposited alumina layer will be stable, adherent, and continuous.
The alumina layer will reduce oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the alumina barrier will prevent or slow substrate oxidation and pesting.
The coating's thinness and strong adhesion will preserve the bulk mechanical properties of the alloy.
Relative to uncoated samples, coated samples will have lower oxidation-induced weight gain after high-temperature exposure.
Relative to uncoated samples, coated samples will form less surface oxide after high-temperature exposure.
Coated samples will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to that of uncoated samples.
Coated samples will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to that of uncoated samples.
Uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr develops pesting and associated surface degradation under the specified high-temperature exposure conditions.
The hypothesis is bounded to five-hour air exposures at 800–1000 °C and mechanical strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
